questions.stem: Which description matches a near coastal voyage, Class 2?
options: A voyage on a lake where the vessel cannot be more than 2.5 nautical miles from shore
Any voyage that is not covered by another class
A voyage that is not sheltered or inland and during which the vessel is always 25 nautical miles or less from shore and 100 nautical miles or less from a place of refuge
A voyage that is always within 200 nautical miles of shore and north of latitude 6 degrees N
questions.explanation: Option one is the Class 2 definition. The 200 nm and 6 degrees N description is Class 1, the 2.5 nm lake or river rule is part of the sheltered waters definition, and 'anything else' is an unlimited voyage.

options: A voyage that is not sheltered, inland, near coastal Class 2 or near coastal Class 1
A voyage of more than 200 nautical miles from shore, and only that
A voyage of more than 24 hours
A voyage by a vessel over 500 gross tonnage
questions.explanation: The regulations define unlimited by exclusion: whatever is not one of the other four classes. Duration and tonnage are not part of it.

questions.stem: A boat on a river above tidal waters cannot be more than 2.5 nautical miles from the nearest shore. What voyage class does this describe?
options: Near coastal, Class 1
Unlimited
Near coastal, Class 2
Sheltered waters
questions.explanation: Paragraph (a) of the sheltered waters voyage definition is a river above tidal waters or a lake where a vessel cannot be more than 2.5 nautical miles from the closest shore.

questions.stem: A passenger vessel holds an inspection certificate for a near coastal voyage, Class 1. Which of these voyages may it also make?
options: Unlimited voyages
Sheltered waters, inland and near coastal Class 2 voyages
Only sheltered waters voyages
Only near coastal Class 1 voyages
questions.explanation: Under s. 14(3) of the Vessel Safety Certificates Regulations a Class 1 certificate also covers sheltered, inland and Class 2. It does not cover unlimited voyages, which is the class above it.

questions.stem: A vessel holds a certificate for a near coastal voyage, Class 2. Which of these voyages does that certificate also cover?
options: Near coastal Class 1 voyages
None; it covers only Class 2
Sheltered waters and inland voyages
Unlimited voyages
questions.explanation: A Class 2 certificate also covers sheltered and inland voyages (s. 14(2)). A certificate for a wider class covers narrower ones, not the other way round.

questions.stem: A charter skipper in BC says: 'The Strait of Georgia is sheltered water.' Which statement is closest to what Schedule 1 says?
options: The Strait is sheltered only from June 1 to September 30
The whole Strait is sheltered because it lies between Vancouver Island and the mainland
The Strait is sheltered anywhere within 25 nautical miles of shore
Only the part of the Strait north of the 49th parallel and east of 123 degrees 22.666 minutes W (excluding Boundary Bay) is listed under Item 7, so the open Strait is not sheltered water
questions.explanation: Item 7 is a defined corner of the Strait with other items carved out. The June 1 to September 30 period belongs to Howe Sound (Item 8), and the 25 nm figure belongs to the Class 2 definition.

questions.stem: A tour boat runs from Squamish into Howe Sound north of the Gower Point to Cape Roger Curtis line. When is that run a sheltered waters voyage under Schedule 1?
options: Only from October 1 to March 31
Only from June 1 to September 30
All year
Never; Howe Sound is not listed
questions.explanation: Item 8 lists Howe Sound north of that line for the period June 1 to September 30 only. Outside those dates it does not qualify under the schedule.

questions.stem: A 12 m boat is run offshore from Tofino at 18 nautical miles from shore, never more than 100 nautical miles from a place of refuge, in waters contiguous to Canada. The waters are not listed in Schedule 1. What voyage class is this?
options: Sheltered waters
Near coastal, Class 2
Near coastal, Class 1
Unlimited
questions.explanation: She is always 25 nm or less from shore and within 100 nm of a place of refuge, and the waters are not sheltered, so the voyage meets the Class 2 definition. Class 1 is the wider class you use when Class 2 does not fit.

questions.stem: Why does the voyage class matter to someone applying for a Master, Limited certificate under 60 gross tonnage?
options: Voyage class has no effect on the certificate
The sea service must be earned on vessels engaged on voyages that correspond to those the certificate vessel is permitted to engage on
The exam pass mark depends on the voyage class
Only unlimited voyage service counts for the certificate
questions.explanation: Section 131 of the Marine Personnel Regulations requires sea service on vessels on voyages that correspond to those of the vessel the certificate is sought for. Pass marks and 'only unlimited' are not in that section.

questions.stem: Which statement about the Class 1 definition is correct?
options: The vessel must always be north of latitude 6 degrees N and within 200 nautical miles of shore or over the continental shelf
The vessel must be on a lake or a river above the tide
The vessel must never leave BC waters
The vessel must always be within 25 nautical miles of shore
questions.explanation: Class 1 is defined by being between listed places, always north of 6 degrees N, and within 200 nm of shore or above the continental shelf. The 25 nm figure is the Class 2 shore limit.
